note: Jersey, read on 2026-10-30 in the Government of Jersey's Work Permit Policy (gov.je, updated January 2026; its fee tables 'accurate as of December 2024'), rendered in a browser because gov.je answers curl with an error. Everyone who isn't British or Irish needs immigration permission to work or settle in Jersey (EU and EEA citizens with settled or pre-settled status and some others excepted); work permits under the Immigration (Work Permits) (Jersey) Rules 1995 are applied for by the employer, are issued to a named employer for a named employee in a specified role, and can't be transferred (work for the sponsor). The long-term work permit (any industry, roles at RQF level 3 or above) is granted for an initial period of up to 3 years (a ceiling, so no term), after which a further permit may be granted; its time counts toward indefinite leave to remain after 5 years' continuous residency; an employee abroad applies for leave to enter through GOV.UK, while one in authorised employment in the UK, Guernsey or the Isle of Man applies for leave to remain in Jersey ('either'). Its permit fee is the employer's and depends on its length (£290 to £350 for one to three years) and the employee's leave to enter or remain is £827 each time, so no single fee is written. The annual temporary permit (construction, sea-going fishing and hospitality) is issued for 12 months, renewable annually up to 36 months (48 for some construction), with a mandatory absence afterwards; its permit fee for more than 9 and up to 12 months is £175 (written; the employee's own leave to enter or remain is £298 more); time on it doesn't count toward settlement. Indefinite leave to remain is applied for in Jersey for £2,885; British citizenship may follow 12 months after it. Decision times aren't stated. The short-term (9-month), student, non-resident and intra-company routes, and dependants, aren't written.

sources.title: Government of Jersey, Work permit policy (updated January 2026)
sources.said: All persons who are not British or Irish require immigration permission to visit, work, study or settle in Jersey. ... Work permits are issued to a named employer, for a named employee to work in a specified role, as detailed on the work permit. Permits cannot be transferred to another employer or employee. ... If your prospective employee is in authorised employment in the UK, Guernsey or Isle of Man they will not need to travel abroad to obtain a separate visa if they are granted a work permit to work in Jersey. ... annual temporary route for construction, sea going fishing sector and hospitality. Permits are issued for periods of 12 months and can be renewed annually ... Time spend on this route doesn’t count to the qualifying period for settlement (indefinite leave to remain). ... This route is available for those individuals employed in any industry for an initial period of up to 3 years following which a further work permit may be granted. ... accrue time towards indefinite leave to remain ... More than 9 months and up to 12 months £175 ... Leave to enter: work permit holder (application via GOV.UK) ... Indefinite Leave to Remain: work permit holder (application in Jersey) ... £2,885 ... Citizenship (12 months after ILR has been granted) ... Long-term work permit: Indefinite leave to remain (5 years continuous residency)
